For a JUMP/RETURN/JUMPT/JUMPF whose target label has a savelab (label_sym +0x12), follows the savelab chain and retargets the branch (and g_current_block's target_labno), adjusts reference counts and the label's block list, and re-runs merge_common_block_tails. For JUMP/RETURN it also retargets earlier JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF blocks that went to labels directly preceding this branch (a JUMP becomes a RETURN when this branch is a RETURN).

name: delete_dead_labels_from_node_list
note: Existing name kept. orig: dellab ("dellab end! labno==%d"). For each block's start label (looked up in g_label_hash) with a zero reference count (when DAT_0042ad40 == 1 and the label kind is 2..5), deletes the LABEL record (after FUN_00414f40 and delete_redundant_conditional_branch) and clears the block's labno.

name: merge_common_block_tails
note: orig: d_comcd (traces "d_comcd start!", "d_comcd end!"). Callers load_next_code_node, rewrite_branch_target_chains, sanitize_node_records_before_branch_rewrite. For a LABEL (0x18), JUMP ('$') or RETURN ('"') record calls find_block_with_common_tail (dc_lbchk). On a match, FUN_00413ce0 builds new node(s) holding the common tail (g_common_tail_a/b, g_common_tail_count) and the new block is linked into the block list (mode 1: after the fall-through block; mode 2: after the current block, with g_last_block updated). The label's block list (label_sym +0x20) is updated and FUN_00415410 fills in the new node. This is the cross-jump pass (XJUMP_OFF in SH5/rebuild/shcpep/src/_pep_rules.c).

name: find_block_with_common_tail
note: orig: dc_lbchk (traces "dc_lbchk end! rc==%d", "make LISTTBL blkptr==%08lx"). Only caller merge_common_block_tails, which uses the low 16 bits as the mode, so the 4-byte return stays. For a JUMP/RETURN ending g_current_block: mode 1 if the target label's block is entered by fall-through from a block with a matching tail (count_common_tail_records(..,1)); mode 2 if another block in the label's branch list (label_sym +0x20) jumps to the same label with a matching tail (count_common_tail_records(..,2)); otherwise the current block is appended to that list. For a LABEL: stores the LABEL psd in label_sym +0x28 and compares each listed jumping block with the fall-through predecessor (mode 1). Outputs the two blocks and the label's block (label psd - 0x10); returns 0 when nothing matches. | return narrowed: callers use the low half (merge_common_block_tails: mode = (short))

name: count_common_tail_records
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: int count_common_tail_records(code_node *block_a, code_node *block_b, psd **tail_a, psd **tail_b, short mode)
note: orig: dc_cmp (traces "dc_cmp start!", "rp==%08lx, r1==%08lx", "dc_cmp end! common code number==%ld"). Only caller find_block_with_common_tail, which stores the results in g_common_tail_count/a/b. block_a must end in JUMP/RETURN with a label operand. Mode 1: block_b must not end in JUMP/RETURN (it falls through) and the comparison starts at its last record. Mode 2: block_b also ends in JUMP/RETURN. Walks both blocks backwards (prefind 00409760) while the records are identical (same per-op payload rules as compare_psd_records, operands via common_code_ea_equal) and do not reference the branch's psd.tmp register (refgchk). Returns the count and the earliest matching record of each block.

name: common_code_ea_equal
note: orig: dc_eacmp (traces "dc_eacmp start!", "dc_eacmp end! rc==%d"). Callers compare_psd_records and count_common_tail_records test the low 16 bits (== 0 / == 1), so the 4-byte return stays. Returns 1 if both are NULL, or if type/base/index/disp are equal and the label_ref lists match element by element (labno1/labno2); else 0. Unlike opeacmp it compares the whole type byte and accepts @-Rn/@Rn+. | return narrowed: callers use the low half ((short) in compare_psd_records, count_common_tail_records)

name: make_common_code_block
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: code_node *make_common_code_block(code_node *block_a, code_node *block_b, psd *common_a, psd *common_b, short mode)
note: Only caller 004131d0 (d_comcd, common-code/cross-jump merge) passes g_common_start_a/b and the mode from 00413490. Allocates ((mode-1+g_common_code_count)/15)+1 nodes (0x178 each, linked by +0c next), gets a new label from make_new_label_number (fatal 0xbc8 if none), creates its label entry (0040a760(2,0x20,labno)), puts a LABEL record in psd[0] (sptravel = g_cur_sptravel), then copies the common records of block_a into the new block with copy_psd_record (skipping SWBGN/SWEND) while deleting them from both blocks (00407d80 delcode). mode 1: block_a's final branch (find_block_final_record) now goes to the new label (RETURN becomes JUMP), block_a->target_labno = new label. mode 2: the final JUMP/RETURN is copied too; block_a's branch is deleted and block_b's branch retargeted to the new label. Returns the new block, or 0 when neither block is in g_current_node_list. Debug strings "make node number = %d", "node number", "code counter".

name: make_new_label_number
note: orig: dc_mklab ("dc_mklab start! g_labno = %ld" / "dc_mklab end! labno = %ld"). Returns ++g_last_labno, or 0 when it would reach 0x8000 or g_label_alloc_disabled == 1. Callers: make_common_code_block, emit_literal_reference_records.

name: copy_psd_record
note: orig: dc_cpycd ("dc_cpycd start! inp=%08lx outp=", input/output psdtbl dumps). Copies op/flg/misc/tmp/sptravel/expno; for CASEJMP, CTBL/CENT, LINE, op 0x10, PROGRAM and the label ops (0x18-0x1b) copies filno..ea2 raw; otherwise copies filno/linno and deep-copies ea1/ea2 with copy_ea (freeing dst's old operands via 0040f6e0 when dst held an ordinary record). An empty src clears dst (0040dc10). Callers include load_next_code_node, advance_sua_record_stream, make_common_code_block, move_record_into_branch_slot.

name: copy_ea
note: orig: cpyea ("cpyea start! eaptr=%08lx", "input eatbl"/"output eatbl", "cpyea end! eap=%08lx"). Allocates a 0xc ea (0040d8a0), copies type/base/index/misc/disp and the label list via copy_label_ref_list. Returns 0 for a null src.

name: copy_label_ref_list
note: orig: cpylab ("cpylab start! lp==%08lx", "input labtbl"/"output labtbl", "cpylab end! newlp==%08lx"). Allocates 8-byte label_refs and copies labno1/labno2 of every element of the list; returns the new head or 0.

name: find_block_final_record
note: (was find_first_branch_record_in_node_chain) orig: dc_bcode ("dc_bcode start! bp=%08lx", "dc_bcode end! np=%08lx scp=%08lx"). EXISTING NAME find_first_branch_record_in_node_chain IS WRONG: inside a node the scan stops at a branch (JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF, EXIT, RETURN, BF/BT/BRA, JMP, RTS/BT_S/BF_S, BRAF, RTE) but then goes on with the next node (+0c) to the end of the chain (disasm 004145e2 -> 00414583), remembering every record that is not DUMMY/BBGN/BEND/LINE. It returns the block's LAST real record (its final branch when it has one; the end trace always prints np=0). Callers check the op afterwards (rewrite_branch_targets_for_node_list, 00409b70, make_common_code_block, delete_branch_to_next_label ...).

name: move_target_block_after_jump
note: orig: str_chg ("str_chg start!", "make LISTTBL node pointer", "LISTTBL chained node pointer", "clear node pointer"). Called from load_next_code_node with LABEL / JUMP / RETURN records. LABEL: stores rec as the label entry's defining record (+0x28). JUMP/RETURN to a not-yet-defined label: records the current block (g_current_block) in the label's jump-source list (+0x20). Then, if the current block starts with a LABEL that an earlier block jumps to, and check_block_move_branches / check_label_movable agree, deletes that jump (00407e70 + 00407d80, target_labno = 0) and relinks the next_block chain so the current block directly follows the jumping block (the blocks in between move after it), runs delete_branch_to_next_label on the following LABEL and updates g_prev_block / g_current_block.

name: check_block_move_branches
note: orig: sc_brchk ("sc_brchk start!", "sc_brchk end! rc = %d"). Returns 1 in the low short (the caller move_target_block_after_jump tests (short)) when jump_source->target_labno == block->labno, block and last_block both have target labels and end in a labelled JUMP (find_block_label_jump), the three jump targets differ, jump_source's target is block's own psd[0] LABEL, and check_label_movable agrees; else 0. 4-byte return kept (Ghidra leaves garbage in the high half). | return narrowed: callers use the low half (move_target_block_after_jump: (short))

name: check_label_movable
note: orig: labchk ("labchk start! labno = %d", "labtype = %d", "labchk end! rc=%d"). Looks the label up in g_label_hash (leaves it in g_label_lookup) and always returns 1: the check is a stub in this release. Callers: move_target_block_after_jump, check_block_move_branches.

name: find_block_label_jump
note: orig: brsrchk ("brsrchk end! cp==%08lx", "brsrchk end! return 0"). Scans the block's nodes for an unconditional JUMP with a label operand and returns it; returns 0 at any other branch, or at SWBGN (g_brsrchk_switch_marker = 1) / SWEND (= -1).

name: delete_switch_markers_in_block
note: Only caller delete_switch_markers_from_cursor. Walks the block's records up to its first branch: SWBGN/SWEND go to delete_switch_marker_pair; after a SWEND it sets g_after_switch_end, and from then on every label record (0x18-0x1b) also goes to delete_switch_marker_pair (which deletes a complete SWBGN/SWEND pair).

name: delete_switch_marker_pair
note: orig: sw_delete ("sw_delete start!", "SWBGN & SWEND delete!", "sw_delete end!"). Keeps a stack of {SWBGN, SWEND} record pairs (g_switch_marker_pairs, depth g_switch_marker_depth): SWBGN pushes, SWEND pops and stores itself; any other record (not CASEJMP) with a complete pair at the current depth sets both markers' op to 0. With g_switch_track_only set it records 0 instead of the records (nothing gets deleted).

name: block_has_non_marker_records
note: Returns 1 when any node of the block holds a record other than DUMMY/LINE/SWBGN/SWEND, else 0. Ghidra returns CONCAT31(garbage,1); the only caller move_target_block_after_jump tests the low byte.

name: delete_branch_to_next_label
note: orig: nxtbrdel ("nxtbrdel start! code pointer = %08lx", "delete code (%08lx) exit number"). label_rec is a block's psd[0] LABEL (block = label_rec - 0x10). Finds the preceding block holding code (00409b70 + block_has_code_records); if its final record (find_block_final_record) is JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF/RETURN to this label, removes that block from the label's jump-source list (JUMP), drops the label references (00407e70) and deletes the branch, clears target_labno; then delete_trailing_branches_to_label. Callers: load_next_code_node, rewrite_branch_target_chains, delete_dead_labels_from_node_list, move_target_block_after_jump, 004152f0.

name: delete_trailing_branches_to_label
note: Only caller delete_branch_to_next_label. Loop: steps back from block to the nearest block with code (block_has_code_records) and, while that block's final record is JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF/RETURN to label_rec's label, deletes it (same steps as nxtbrdel), so "bt L; bra L; L:" loses both branches.

name: block_has_code_records
note: Returns 1 when the block holds a record other than DUMMY/SWBGN/SWEND/LINE/LABEL/CLABEL/DLABEL. Ghidra returns CONCAT31(garbage,1); every caller tests the low byte: load_next_code_node, delete_branch_to_next_label, delete_trailing_branches_to_label, delete_redundant_conditional_branch.

name: rewrite_branch_targets_for_node_list
note: Existing name kept: for every block with a target_labno whose final record (find_block_final_record) is JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF/RETURN it sets g_whole_list_pass = 1, g_prev_block, g_current_block and calls rewrite_branch_target_chains. First whole-list pass in optimize_current_node_list.

name: clean_records_and_merge_common_code
note: (was sanitize_node_records_before_branch_rewrite) EXISTING NAME IS MISLEADING: optimize_current_node_list calls it AFTER rewrite_branch_targets_for_node_list. It runs delete_switch_markers_from_cursor, then for every record up to each node's first branch: sanitize_record_for_serialization (dropping a label whose record vanished: 00409a70/00407f00/004099f0/00409a50), and for each LABEL the common-code merge 004131d0 (d_comcd) and delete_branch_to_next_label; finally sanitizes a copy of the 0x18-byte record at 00429bd0 as a LABEL. Suggest clean_records_and_merge_common_code. Signature unchanged.

name: compute_block_sptravel_delta
note: Only caller 004131d0 (d_comcd), which stores the result in the merged block's psd[0].sptravel (+0x14). Walks the block (each node up to a branch) summing stack effects: @r15+ / @-r15 operands (00407690 = operand size), CALL to a runtime routine (labno < 0xb7) adds g_runtime_call_sptravel[labno], ADD/SUB #imm,r15 (directly or through the MOVI found by 00409760); LABEL resets the sum to 0. Returns |sptravel - sum|. The sum starts as the block pointer but the block always starts with a LABEL that zeroes it.

name: delete_switch_markers_from_cursor
note: Advances g_switch_scan_block (to g_current_node_list when 0, else ->next_block) and runs delete_switch_markers_in_block on it; when g_switch_track_only is 0 it continues over all following blocks. Callers: 0040ea50 (emission, with g_switch_track_only = 1), move_target_block_after_jump, 004152f0.

name: invert_cond_branch_over_jump
note: (was delete_redundant_conditional_branch) orig: d_condbr ("d_condbr start!", "delete code (%08lx) exit number"). EXISTING NAME IS MISLEADING: for "bcond L; <unlabelled block ending in JUMP/RETURN M>; L:" it inverts the conditional branch (JUMPT <-> JUMPF), retargets it to M, moves the target label, unlinks the jump block from M's jump-source list and deletes the unconditional jump. Suggest invert_cond_branch_over_jump. Callers: load_next_code_node, delete_dead_labels_from_node_list.

name: fill_branch_delay_slots
note: (was rewrite_branch_test_records_with_masks) EXISTING NAME rewrite_branch_test_records_with_masks IS WRONG: this is the delay-slot filling pass (optimize_current_node_list calls it just before emit_backend_record_streams; notes/shcpep.md: NOPing it changes the .sub). For each branch-type record (EXIT/RETURN/CALL/JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF/RTE/BRA/BSR/JMP/JSR/RTS/BSRF/BRAF) it finds the previous movable record (find_previous_branch_rewrite_anchor), sets the branch's register use/def masks (g_branch_uses_lo/hi, g_branch_defs_lo/hi from g_reg_masks: target/call register, PR for calls, T for conditional branches and RTE, the epilogue's registers via add_epilogue_register_masks for EXIT/RETURN), steps over the T-setting compare before a JUMPT/JUMPF (accumulate_compare_test_record_masks) and calls validate_branch_rewrite_masks; a JUMPT/JUMPF with nothing movable before it goes to rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence (fill from the target). JUMPT/JUMPF only when request +0x18 is set; EXIT/RETURN only when classify_branch_rewrite_mode != 0.

name: add_epilogue_register_masks
note: Only caller fill_branch_delay_slots (EXIT, and RETURN with mode < 2). From the current function's aux record (g_aux_record_table + g_current_function_index*0x44): a non-zero frame (+0 plus +0x24) adds r15 and memory to the branch uses/defs (>= 0x80 also r1); unless aux +0xb & 0x80 adds PR; aux +0x17 bit 0, +8 bit 0, +8 bit 1 add r15 plus registers 0x65/0x67/0x68: the registers the epilogue restores, which the slot record must not touch.

name: classify_branch_rewrite_mode
note: Name acceptable; more precise: classify_return_slot_mode. For EXIT, or RETURN with fewer than 2 saved registers (count_function_saved_registers): 0 when aux +0xa & 0x3800; 1 when no saved registers and (no aux 0x8000 flag or a zero frame); else 0. Otherwise returns the saved-register count. fill_branch_delay_slots skips the slot when 0 and adds epilogue masks when < 2.

name: count_function_saved_registers
note: Counts set bits in the current function's aux record (g_current_function_index*0x44): +4 (16 bits), +0x17 (2 bits), +6 (16 bits), +8 (2 bits), the registers the prologue/epilogue save and restore. Callers: classify_branch_rewrite_mode, 00410630 (tests > 1).

name: find_previous_slot_candidate
note: (was find_previous_branch_rewrite_anchor) Name vague; more precise: find_previous_slot_candidate. From rec steps backwards (00409760) over non-instructions (ADD #0 without label, CASEJMP, LINE, DUMMY, CTBL/CENT, SWBGN/SWEND, ENTER, label ops) until node->psd[0]; returns the first real instruction, or 0 when it is a call (JSR/BSR/CALL/BSRF) or still a non-instruction. Used by fill_branch_delay_slots and validate_branch_rewrite_masks.

name: select_delay_slot_record
note: (was validate_branch_rewrite_masks) EXISTING NAME IS MISLEADING (it chooses and marks the slot record, it does not just validate); suggest select_delay_slot_record. Walks backwards from cand (via find_previous_branch_rewrite_anchor): computes each record's register uses (g_cand_uses_lo/hi) and defs (g_cand_defs_lo/hi) incl. memory/T/GBR/r15, stops when 00419500 says so; when delay_slot_masks_disjoint holds (and the SLOT_NO_STACK rule of _pep_rules.c does not reject a frame access) it marks the record flg |= 0x40 (goes into the next branch's slot) and the following JUMPT/JUMPF misc |= 0x80 (delayed form) and returns 1; otherwise it ORs the record's masks into the branch masks and tries the previous record. Returns 0 when none qualifies. Caller fill_branch_delay_slots.

name: delay_slot_masks_disjoint
note: Returns 1 when the candidate's defs do not meet the branch window's uses and the candidate's uses do not meet its defs (g_cand_defs_lo & g_branch_uses_lo, g_cand_defs_hi & g_branch_uses_hi, g_cand_uses_lo & g_branch_defs_lo, g_cand_uses_hi & g_branch_defs_hi all zero), else 0. Callers validate_branch_rewrite_masks and rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence use only the byte.

name: accumulate_compare_test_record_masks
note: Existing name kept. For a T-setting record (CMP/EQ..CMP/STR 0x50-0x57, TST, DT, ops 0xc0/0xc1/0xc7) adds T to the branch uses/defs plus the record's register operands (GBR and memory for TST #imm,@(R0,GBR)) and returns 1; else 0. Caller fill_branch_delay_slots tests the byte.

name: fill_cond_branch_slot_from_target
note: (was rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence) orig: delaymov ("delaymov start!", "delaymov end!"). Existing name vague; suggest fill_cond_branch_slot_from_target. For a JUMPT/JUMPF to label L whose fall-through block has no label and is followed by L's block (or by an unlabelled block that jumps to a second once-referenced label): if L is referenced once, takes the first movable record after L (find_slot_candidate_after_label), checks it against the branch masks (delay_slot_masks_disjoint; SLOT_NO_STACK hook in the rebuild) and against every record of the fall-through block(s) (none may be CASEJMP/CALL/JSR/BSR/BSRF), then move_record_into_branch_slot and adjust_label_sptravel_for_moved_record. Ghidra's sig has no return value (the rebuild declares int).

name: move_record_into_branch_slot
note: orig: mvcode ("mvcode start!", "mvcode end!"). In node's last node finds branch; the record after it (or a newly allocated node when the branch is at index >= 14) must be empty: copies the branch there, copies cand into the branch's old place and deletes cand from the target block (00407d80); marks the moved record flg |= 0x40 and the branch misc |= 0x80 (the marks validate_branch_rewrite_masks uses). Caller rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence.

name: find_slot_candidate_after_label
note: Only caller rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence (label_rec = the label entry's defining record, +0x28). Returns the first real record after label_rec (skipping ADD #0, DUMMY, LINE, CTBL/CENT, SWBGN/SWEND), or 0 when it is a branch/call/RTE/CASEJMP/ENTER/op 0xa0/0x30/0x31, a MOVI that 00409ad0 rejects, or an unlabelled MOVI that ends the block.

name: adjust_label_sptravel_for_moved_record
note: Only caller rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence, after the move. Computes rec's stack effect (@r15+ / @-r15 operand size via 00407690, ADD #imm,r15) and adds it to psd[0].sptravel of target_block and second_block when their psd[0] is LABEL/CLABEL/DLABEL.

name: dump_memory_hex
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: int dump_memory_hex(unsigned char *addr, char *title, int size)
note: Debug hex dump: prints the address and title, then size bytes in rows of 16 via dump_hex_line; prints the "<<<...*00000000 ADDRESS..." message for a null address. Callers pass records with titles such as "dc_cpycd : input psdtbl dmp" and sizes 0x18/0xc/8 (copy_psd_record, copy_ea, copy_label_ref_list, 00403200, 00409840, 00413bb0). Returns the last row's result (0).

name: dump_hex_line
note: One row of dump_memory_hex: count bytes as "%02x", padding to 0x12 columns, then the printable characters (others as a placeholder). Returns 0.

name: decide_literal_pool_placement
note: (was emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record) Existing name kept, but it is imprecise: the function emits no pool entries. It is the literal-pool placement rule. It collects the literals each record needs into three hash tables (g_word_literal_table 00429570, g_long_literal_table 00429780, g_frame_offset_literal_table 00429990) and adds their sizes to g_pool_pending_literal_bytes (2 or 4 each). It adds the record's code size (compute_record_code_size) to g_pool_code_bytes. At branch records (RTS 0x96, RTE 0x8e, BRA 0x92, JMP 0x94, JUMP 0x24, EXIT 0x21, RETURN 0x22) it writes a 1-byte decision (1 = place the pool after this branch) to the .lit stream: flush when code+pool > limit-0x30, limit 0x1fe with word literals pending, else 0x3fc. It forces a flush past 0x1ce/0x3cc in straight code. Returns (pool bytes + 2) in the low 16 bits, or 0; callers (emit_backend_record_streams, FUN_0040ea50) use (short). Suggested name: decide_literal_pool_placement. lit_out = g_lit_output at both call sites.

name: find_pool_literal
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: int find_pool_literal(literal_table *table, unsigned int value, label_ref *labels)
note: Hashes value + every labno1/labno2 of labels mod 0x7f. Walks the bucket chain (table+0xc+4*hash, chained by entry+4) and calls pool_literal_matches. Returns 1 if an equal literal is already pending, else 0. Callers pass 0x429570/0x429780/0x429990 (the literal tables). table would be literal_table * (types_proposal.h).

name: pool_literal_matches
note: 1 if entry->value (+8) == value and entry's label list (+0xc) holds the same labno1/labno2 set as labels (each one matched once via a 20-flag scratch array), else 0. Only caller is find_pool_literal. entry would be literal_entry *.

name: add_pool_literal
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void add_pool_literal(literal_table *table, unsigned int value, label_ref *labels)
note: Allocates a 0x10-byte entry (FUN_00407890(0x10)) with value at +8 and a copy of the label list (8-byte nodes) at +0xc. Links it into hash bucket (value + labnos) % 0x7f (chain +4) and onto the table's insertion list (head +0, tail +4), and increments count +8. Callers: emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record, second pass.

name: clear_pool_literal_table
note: Frees every entry (FUN_00407c30(e,0x10)) and its label nodes (8 bytes each), zeroes the 0x7f buckets, then head/tail/count. Reports internal error 0x12f2 if the freed count != table->count (+8). Called at every pool flush.

name: write_final_literal_pool_flag
note: Writes one byte 1 (= place pool) to the .lit stream; error 0xce7 on failure. Called once by shcpep_main just before closing g_lit_output.

name: is_word_symbol_literal
note: 1 if labels is a single symbol (labno2 == 0) for which FUN_00409c50 returns nonzero (the "address fits a word literal" test; emit_literal_pool puts those in the word table). value is unused. Caller: emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record, MOVA_PC/MOVI cases.

name: get_marked_symbol_kind
note: If labels is one node with labno2 == -0x8000, returns FUN_00409ca0(labno1) (symbol attribute bits & 3), else 0. Callers compare the full value (==1: no pool literal needed; ==0: long literal). Ghidra's sig says undefined (void), but the disassembly returns EAX and callers use it, so int is proposed: LEAD DECIDE.

name: accumulate_operand_register_masks
note: which 1 = ea1, 2 = ea2. ORs the registers the operand reads or writes into g_record_regs_touched_lo/hi (00429c40/44) and those it modifies (pre-decrement, post-increment, or a direct register the record changes per FUN_00408120 "regchgchk") into g_record_regs_written_lo/hi (0042ad58/5c), via g_register_mask_table (00425ff8, registers >= 0x60 go to the _hi word). EA kinds 10/11/12 add the PC/GBR bits. Bad EA kind: internal error 0x127b. Callers: compute_record_register_masks, validate_branch_rewrite_masks, FUN_00405a80.

name: is_register_scan_barrier
note: 1 for LDC (0x8c) to control register 0x61 or 0x63, and for TRAPA (0x9e) / SLEEP (0x9f), else 0. Register scans stop here. Callers test the low byte only: validate_branch_rewrite_masks (loop exit) and compute_record_register_masks.

name: accumulate_t_bit_masks
note: Adds T (register 0x61, mask 0042617c) to the touched mask, and to the written mask for T-setting ops: SHAL/SHLL/ROTx/CMP/ADDC/... (0x48..0x79 minus the non-T list), CASEJMP, TST/TAS/DT/CLRT/RTE/SETT, 0xc0/0xc1/0xc7. Ops that only read T (JUMPT/JUMPF, MOVT, BF/BT, BT/S, BF/S, TRAPA) add touched only. Only caller: accumulate_special_register_masks.

name: accumulate_special_register_masks
note: MUL/MULS/MULU (0x6f-0x71) add MACL (reg 0x65); MAC (0x72) and CLRMAC (0x9b) add MACH (0x64) and MACL, each to both touched and written. Every other op goes to accumulate_t_bit_masks. Callers: compute_record_register_masks, validate_branch_rewrite_masks.

name: compute_record_register_masks
note: Clears the four g_record_regs_* masks, then fills them for one record. Per-op cases: ENTER/EXIT/CALL/JUMP*/MOV_LOC/MOVA*/0x2c/0x2e/CMP/TST/DT/JSR/BSR/RTS..., including PR (0x66), r15 and MACH/MACL clobbered by calls when request->macsave (+0x36) == 0. Then it handles the operands (accumulate_operand_register_masks) and accumulate_special_register_masks. Returns 1 for NULL/OP_NON_10/SLEEP and for scan barriers (is_register_scan_barrier), and 0 for directives (op < 0x10, 0x14..0x1f) and ADD #0. Callers test the low byte (rewrite_delay_move_branch_sequence, FUN_0040fb20, FUN_00411ed0, FUN_004120d0, FUN_00405a80).

name: move_psd_record
note: Frees dst's operands (FUN_0040f6e0) unless dst is a label/CTBL/CENT/LINE/CASEJMP/OP_NON_10/PROGRAM directive. Copies op/flg/misc/tmp/sptravel/expno and the op-dependent tail (+0xc..+0x17) from src to dst, transferring operand ownership. Then clears src to an empty record (op 0, tmp 0xff). Only caller: FUN_00405a80.

name: compute_record_code_size
note: (was measure_serialized_record_size) EXISTING NAME IS WRONG: this is the SH target code size in bytes of the record, not its .sub size. Base value from g_op_code_size_table (00427c80, short per op: MOV=2, BRA/RTS=4 with delay slot, CALL=6, JUMPT=10, CASEJMP=58). Adjusted for CTBL (count*4), OP_NON_10 data (even length + 2), ENTER/EXIT/RETURN (2 bytes per saved register from count_saved_registers, frame adjust 2 or 4), MOV_LOC (g_mov_loc_size_table by displacement range) and flag 0x40 (-2). Low 16 bits = size; callers use (short) (load_next_code_node sums it, emit_backend_record_streams, emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record). Suggested name: compute_record_code_size. | return narrowed: callers use the low half (sizes added as short, written as bytes)

name: count_saved_registers
note: Counts the set bits of the aux record's two 16-bit register masks (+4, +6) of g_aux_record_table[aux_index] (0x44-byte records), adjusted by flags +0xa (0x4000/0x1800), +0x17 bits 1/2 and +8 bits 1/2 (extra saved specials). Low 16 bits used ((short)) by callers: compute_record_code_size (2 bytes per push), frame_offset_to_sp_displacement (4 bytes each), emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record (RETURN case, < 2). The count is a 16-bit counter and every caller reads its low half ((short)).

name: frame_offset_to_sp_displacement
note: Returns aux.frame_size (+0 of g_aux_record_table[g_current_aux_index]) + sp_travel + frame_offset, plus 4*count_saved_registers (+4 if aux+0xb bit 0x80 clear) for frame_offset >= 0, or just +4 for a negative offset. Callers pass ea->disp and psd.sptravel of MOV_LOC/MOVA_LC records (compute_record_code_size, emit_literal_pool_entries_for_record).

name: write_sub_record
note: Resets g_sub_filno=1, g_sub_linno=0 and g_sub_report_extra_arg=0, then writes the op byte and dispatches on g_sub_record_format_table[op][0] (00427ec0): 1 write_sub_machine_op_record, 2 casejmp, 3 ctbl, 4 cent, 5 label, 6 line, 7 nothing, 8 write_sub_instruction_record, 9 op10, 10 section. op > 0xf1 or format 0: error 0x1318; bad format: 0x1319.

name: write_sub_casejmp_record
note: Format 2 (OP_CASEJMP only): expno (+8, 4), filno (+0xc, 2), linno (+0xe, 2), +0x10 (4), +0x14 (4) via write_sub_bytes.

name: write_sub_cent_record
note: Format 4 (OP_CENT only): 2 bytes at +0x10.

name: write_sub_ctbl_record
note: Format 3 (OP_CTBL only): the shorts at +0xc (entry count; compute_record_code_size uses it *4) and +0xe.

name: write_sub_label_record
note: Format 5 (LABEL/CLABEL/DLABEL/FLABEL): the label number (+0x10, 2 bytes) and sptravel (+4, 4 bytes).

name: write_sub_line_record
note: Format 6 (OP_LINE only): sets g_sub_filno/g_sub_linno from filno/linno, then writes filno (2), linno (2) and 1 byte at +0x10.

name: write_sub_machine_op_record
note: Format 1 (every SH machine op, MOV..0xf1): sets g_sub_filno/linno and writes filno, linno, expno, flg, misc and the operand count. The count must equal g_sub_record_format_table[op][1], else error 0x1310. Then each operand via write_sub_operand(out, ea, flg & 3).

name: write_sub_operand
note: Existing name and signature kept.

name: count_label_ref_markers
note: Counts labno1/labno2 fields equal to -0x8000 (0x8000) in the list. write_sub_operand requires exactly one on a labelled @(disp,GBR) operand (else error 0x1311).

name: write_sub_label_list
note: Writes a 4-byte count of the nonzero labno1/labno2 values (stopping at the first 0), then each one as 2 bytes. Called after every operand value in write_sub_operand.

name: write_sub_instruction_record
note: Existing name and signature kept. Format 8: the pseudo instructions ENTER/EXIT/RETURN/CALL/JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF/MOV_LOC/MOVA_LC/MOVA_PC/MOVI/MOVA_FC/0x2c/0x2e/0x30/0x31.

name: write_sub_op10_record
note: Format 9 (OP_NON_10 only): sets g_sub_filno/linno and writes filno, linno, +0x10 (4) and +0x14 (4). +0x14 is the length that compute_record_code_size rounds up to even + 2.

name: write_sub_section_record
note: Format 10 (PROGRAM/CONST/DATA/BSS): the 2-byte section number at +0xc. This is the id that find_request_section (0040fae0) looks up in request->sections.

name: write_sub_bytes
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void write_sub_bytes(FILE *out, char *buf, unsigned int n)
note: write_file_bytes(out, buf, n). On -1 it reports 0xce7 (cannot output) through FUN_00410e90(g_sub_filno, g_sub_linno, ...). An extra 5th argument g_sub_report_extra_arg is pushed (FUN_00410e90 takes 4). Used by every write_sub_* helper.

name: read_file_bytes
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned int read_file_bytes(FILE *in, char *buf, unsigned int n)
note: fread(buf,1,n,in) (via __fread_lk). Returns -1 for a NULL file/buffer or n < 1. When nothing was read: 0 at a clean EOF (_flag 0x10 without 0x20), else -1. Used by the request loader, the request trailer copy and others.

name: write_file_bytes
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned int write_file_bytes(FILE *out, char *buf, unsigned int n)
note: fwrite(buf, n, 1, out) (FUN_0041e8d0). Returns n, or -1 on failure, a NULL file/buffer or n < 1. Shared by every stage writer: request store, .lit decision bytes, message records.

name: store_request_record_file
note: Existing name. stage is unused (shcpep_main passes 3). Opens path "wb" and writes the short g_request_fixed_size, the raw fixed part (write_request_fixed_part), the variable part (write_request_variable_part) and the saved trailer (copy_request_trailer_from_temp) if any. Then frees g_request_record_path. Errors 0xce4/0xce5 -> stock_exit(9). The return value's low 16 bits are 0 (upper half = stock_free's EAX); shcpep_main tests (short)==-1. request would be request *. Returns XOR AX,AX (0) after the final free; low half: shcpep_main tests (short) == -1, handle_fault_signal ignores it.

name: check_request_write_result
note: result == -1 -> report_message_by_code(request->source_name, 0, 0xce7 cannot output) and stock_exit(9). Used after every request-store write.

name: write_request_fixed_part
note: Writes the first g_request_fixed_size bytes of the request verbatim (pointer fields included; the loader overwrites them).

name: write_request_variable_part
note: Writes the string count 0x1e (30), then the 30 counted strings (fields +0x00, +0x38, +0x3c, +0x50..+0xa8, +0x114, +0x140, +0x11c, +0x120), then the lists +0x24, +0x40, +0x48, +0x4c, +0xec, +0xb8, +0xbc, +0xc0, the +0x144 block and the string +0x15c. Mirror of read_request_variable_part. request would be request *.

name: write_request_string
note: Writes short (strlen+1) and the bytes including the NUL, or a short 0 for NULL.

name: write_request_section_list
note: Writes the count of the 0x20-byte section records (chained by +0x1c) at request+0x24, then each record raw (0x20 bytes) followed by its name (+4) of length +2 plus 1.

name: write_request_string_list_040
note: Writes count + counted strings of a {next, char *} list. Called for request+0x40 (read back by read_request_string_list_040, 8-byte nodes). Same code as write_request_string_list_048.

name: write_request_string_list_048
note: Same code as write_request_string_list_040, called for request+0x48 (12-byte nodes on load).

name: write_request_sized_string_list
note: List at request+0x4c, nodes {next, char *str, short len-1}: count, then each string as short (len+1) plus bytes.

name: write_request_source_file_list
note: List at request+0xec, nodes {next, short filno, short len, char *name}: count, then 4 bytes (filno, strlen+1) and the name. report_message_by_code and FUN_00410e90 map file names to and from numbers through this list.

name: write_request_11byte_entry_list
note: Lists at request+0xb8 and +0xbc, 16-byte nodes: count, then 11 bytes per node (+4..+7, +0xc, +0xe, +0xf, +8..+0xb). Mirror of read_request_11byte_entry_list. Meaning of the entries unknown.

name: write_request_12byte_entry_list
note: List at request+0xc0, 16-byte nodes: count, then 12 bytes per node (+8..+0xb, +4..+7, +0xc..+0xf). Mirror of read_request_12byte_entry_list.

name: write_request_cpp_block
note: Block at request+0x144: writes the short g_request_cpp_block_size and, if nonzero, the raw block, the string count 5 and the 5 counted strings at block+4..+0x14. Mirror of read_request_cpp_block.

name: copy_request_trailer_from_temp
note: Rewinds g_request_trailer_file and copies it byte by byte to out (the request file being stored). Clears the pointer and calls close_and_delete_temp_files. Caller: store_request_record_file when a trailer was saved.

name: load_request_record_file
note: Existing name. Opens path "rb" and reads the short fixed size into g_request_fixed_size. Allocates the request (stock_malloc), reads the fixed part and the variable part, picks the SHC_/SHCPP_ env names from request+0x144 and saves the trailer for this stage. Sets g_loaded_request and request->stage (+0x118) = stage. Errors 0xce4/0xbcd/0xce5, and 0xceb when g_request_version_mismatch. Copies path to g_request_record_path. Returns the request (would be request *).

name: check_request_read_result
note: result 0 or -1 -> report_message_by_code(NULL, 0, 0xce6 cannot input) and stock_exit(9). Used after every request-load read.

name: read_request_fixed_part
note: Reads g_request_fixed_size bytes into the request.

name: read_request_variable_part
note: Reads the string count, then the 30 counted strings into the same fields write_request_variable_part writes. If request+0x144 (C++ block) is 0, compares +0x11c with "SH SERIES C Compiler Ver. 5.0(Release26)" and +0x120 with the Hitachi copyright and sets g_request_version_mismatch on a difference. A count != 0x1e: error 0x12c1, stock_exit(11). Then reads the lists +0x24, +0x40, +0x48, +0x4c, +0xec, +0xb8, +0xbc, +0xc0, the +0x144 block and string +0x15c.

name: read_request_string
note: Reads a short length; if nonzero, stock_malloc(len) and reads the bytes into *field, else *field = NULL. 0xbcd on allocation failure.

name: read_request_section_list
note: Reads a count of 0x20-byte section records (each stock_malloc(0x20)), each followed by its name (length +2, plus 1). Sets +4 = name, clears +0x18 and next (+0x1c), and appends in order. Read back into request+0x24.

name: read_request_string_list_040
note: Count + counted strings into 8-byte nodes {next, char *}. A zero length is error 0x12c2 (stock_exit 11). For request+0x40.

name: read_request_string_list_048
note: Same as read_request_string_list_040 with 12-byte nodes (+8 left unset) and error 0x12c3. For request+0x48.

name: read_request_sized_string_list
note: 12-byte nodes {next, char *str, short len-1}; a zero length is error 0x12c3. For request+0x4c.

name: read_request_source_file_list
note: 12-byte nodes {next, short filno, short name_len, char *name}, read as 4 bytes (filno, len) then the name. A zero length is error 0x12c4. For request+0xec.

name: read_request_11byte_entry_list
note: Reads a count of 11-byte entries into 16-byte nodes (stock_malloc(0x10)): bytes 0-3 -> +4..+7, 4-6 -> +0xc, +0xe, +0xf, 7-10 -> +8..+0xb. Appends in order. For request+0xb8 and +0xbc.

name: read_request_12byte_entry_list
note: Reads a count of 12-byte entries into 16-byte nodes: bytes 0-3 -> +8..+0xb, 4-7 -> +4..+7, 8-11 -> +0xc..+0xf. For request+0xc0.

name: read_request_cpp_block
note: Reads a short size; if nonzero, sets g_request_cpp_block_size, stock_malloc(size), reads the raw block and a count, then 5 counted strings into block+4..+0x14, and stores the block pointer. Nonzero at request+0x144 means C++ (SHCPP_* env names, no version check).

name: save_request_trailer_to_temp
note: If bytes follow the request in the file and stage != 5, opens a temp file (open_temp_file) as g_request_trailer_file and copies the rest of the file into it, else sets that to NULL. Caller: load_request_record_file. copy_request_trailer_from_temp writes it back on store.

name: configure_signal_handlers
note: Existing name. mode != 1 installs handlers for SIGINT(2), SIGBREAK(0x15), SIGILL(4), SIGABRT(0x16) and SIGSEGV(0xb). Source shcpsig.c.

name: handle_interrupt_signal
note: CREATE: not a function in the analysis (only configure_signal_handlers pushes its address). The SIGINT handler: close_and_delete_temp_files, then exit(13). As shcasm 004329a0.

name: handle_fault_signal
note: CREATE: not a function in the analysis (only configure_signal_handlers pushes its address). The handler of SIGBREAK/SIGILL/SIGABRT/SIGSEGV (0x15, 4, 0x16, 0xb): close_and_delete_temp_files; for a C++ request (g_loaded_request->cpp_block) of stage 0 with errors and message_flags bit 0 clear it stores the request back (store_request_record_file(0, g_request_record_path)) and exits 7; else exit(15). As shcasm 004329b0.

name: emit_progress_banner
note: Existing name. fputs(g_progress_banner_table[stage]) + newline to stderr (00428510) and fflush. Source shcptitl.c.

name: open_temp_file
note: Returns NULL if 8 temp files are already open. Otherwise builds make_temp_file_name() + ".tmp", opens it "wb+" (0xce4 on failure) and records {path, FILE*} in g_temp_files[g_temp_file_count++]. Returns the FILE*. Ghidra's int is a pointer. Source shcptmp.c.

name: close_and_delete_temp_files
note: For each g_temp_files entry: fclose (0xce5), delete the file (FUN_00423aa0, 0xce8 cannot delete), free the path. Then g_temp_file_count = 0. Also called on fatal exits.

name: make_temp_file_name
note: Directory from get_env_directory(g_tmp_env_name) ("" if unset; 0xcf9 if too long). Then sprintf("%s%d.%d", dir, abs(GetCurrentProcessId()), g_temp_name_counter++) into a stock_malloc'd buffer sized from tmpnam and the pid digit count. Returns g_temp_name_buffer.

name: report_message_by_code
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: short report_message_by_code(char *file_name, int line, int msgno, char *text)
note: Name taken from shcasm's 00434550. Looks file_name up in request->source_files (+0xec) for its number. Appends a record (short msgno, int line, short 0, short filno, byte len, text <= 255) to the message file request+0x60 ("ab"). This happens when msgno/1000 > 0, request+0x124 & 8, or request+0x14a == 1. Write failures go to report_message_file_error_and_exit. Counts: msgno/1000 0 -> +0x160, 1|5 -> warning_count +0xc8, 2|6 -> error_count +0xcc. Nothing if no request is loaded. Callers ignore the return value (low 16 bits are 0). Source shcpmsc2.c. It returns 0 in AX (the high half is whatever EAX held), the low half; no caller reads the result.

name: report_message_file_error_and_exit
note: Prints "\n  <source>(0) : <msgno> " to stdout (004284f0) plus "Internal error" for 4xxx or the 33xx "(F) Cannot open/close/input/output internal file" text (table at 004283c8). Then close_and_delete_temp_files and stock_exit(0x29 or 0x2b). Only caller: report_message_by_code.

name: get_env_directory
note: getenv(var_name) copied into the static buffer g_env_directory (at most 0x74 chars) with a trailing '\\' added if missing. Returns NULL if the variable is unset (*ok = 1) or too long (*ok = 0). An empty value returns "". Caller: make_temp_file_name (var = SHC_TMP or SHCPP_TMP).

name: select_env_variable_names
note: Sets g_inc_env_name/g_tmp_env_name/g_lib_env_name* to "SHC_INC"/"SHC_TMP"/"SHC_LIB" (0) or "SHCPP_INC"/"SHCPP_TMP"/"SHCPP_LIB". Caller: load_request_record_file with request+0x144 != 0.

name: _printf
note: Library printf (Ghidra FID_conflict:_wprintf, VS98 _printf): __stbuf/_output/__ftbuf on stdout 004284f0. Used by every debug trace.

name: stock_malloc
note: CRT malloc: stock_nh_malloc(size, _newmode 004287a8). Ghidra's sig says undefined (void), but it returns stock_nh_malloc's EAX and every caller uses the pointer: LEAD DECIDE (void *).

name: stock_nh_malloc
note: CRT _nh_malloc: NULL if size > 0xffffffe0, size 0 becomes 1. Loops stock_heap_alloc, calling the new handler (FUN_0041fdf0) while call_new_handler and the handler succeeds. Ghidra's int is the pointer.

name: stock_heap_alloc
note: CRT _heap_alloc: HeapAlloc(_crtheap 0042af50, 0, size). Ghidra's sig says undefined, but the value is returned in EAX and stock_nh_malloc uses it: LEAD DECIDE (void *).

name: stock_free
note: CRT free: HeapFree(_crtheap, 0, p) if p. store_request_record_file returns this call's EAX & 0xffff0000 (low half 0, the only part callers test), so void is safe.

name: _fclose
note: Library fclose (FID match). Keep the library name.

name: stock_calloc
note: CRT calloc: HeapAlloc(_crtheap, HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY, count*size) with the new-handler retry loop. Callers: load_symbol_aux_record_stream (0x2c and 0x44 record arrays).

name: __fsopen
note: Library _fsopen (FID match). Keep the library name.

name: open_shared_file
note: Existing name. __fsopen(path, mode, 0x40 = _SH_DENYNO). Ghidra's sig says undefined, but it returns __fsopen's FILE* in EAX and every caller uses it: LEAD DECIDE (FILE *).

name: stock_cinit
note: CRT _cinit: calls _FPinit (0042bf68) if set, then _initterm over the C initializers (00425008..00425010) and C++ initializers (00425000..00425004) via FUN_0041e620.

name: stock_exit
note: CRT exit: FUN_0041e5a0(code, 0, 0) = _doexit. Used for every fatal stop (9, 11, ...) and by shcpep_main's normal exit(1).

name: stock_doexit
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void stock_doexit(int exit_code, int quick, int retcaller)
note: CRT doexit (crt0dat.c, static). Sets _C_Exit_Done=1 and _exitflag=(char)retcaller; if !quick runs the onexit table __onexitend-4 down to __onexitbegin, then _initterm(__xp_a,__xp_z); always _initterm(__xt_a,__xt_z); ExitProcess(code) unless retcaller. Caller ___exit passes (code,1,0). Compiled in rebuild src -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_initterm
note: CRT _initterm(_PVFV *pfbegin, _PVFV *pfend) (crt0dat.c, static): calls each non-null function pointer in [begin,end). Called by doexit with __xp_a/__xp_z and __xt_a/__xt_z. Params are pointer-to-function-pointer (no allowed type), so no signature. Compiled -> stock_ prefix. Parameter names from the CRT source; the export's widths and types.

name: __amsg_exit
note: Kept (FID: crt0dat.c). Parameter names from the CRT source; the export's widths and types.

name: __fwrite_lk
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned int __fwrite_lk(char *buf, unsigned int size, unsigned int count, FILE *stream)
note: CRT fwrite body (fwrite.c; single-thread libc, so this IS fwrite; same body as _fwrite_lk, named to match the existing __fread_lk). Copies into _ptr/_cnt, __flsbuf for single chars while the rest is smaller than the buffer, __flush then _write for whole buffers, sets _IOERR (0x20). Caller FUN_0041c050. Not compiled: _crt_shim.c defines FUN_0041e8d0 as fwrite(); rename that shim definition (C name __fwrite_lk -> symbol ___fwrite_lk, no libc collision).

name: _signal
note: Kept (library name; excluded, replaced by _crt_shim.c _signal). SIG: two parameters (every caller pushes the signal number and the handler; Ghidra's one-parameter form made the rebuild register garbage). As shcasm 00435cd0.

name: siglookup
note: Kept (FID: signal.c static). Parameter names from the CRT source; the export's widths and types.

name: stock_flsall
note: CRT flsall (fflush.c, static): walks __piob[0..511] (0x800 bytes), _fflush on in-use streams (_flag & 0x83); FLUSHALL (1) returns the count, FFLUSHNULL (0) only write streams and returns -1 on any error. Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: init_namebuf
note: Kept (FID: tmpnam.c static). Parameter names from the CRT source; the export's widths and types.

name: genfname
note: Kept (FID: tmpnam.c static). Parameter names from the CRT source; the export's widths and types.

name: __output
note: CRT _output (output.c): the printf engine. __lookuptable state machine (states at 0x00424010, char class at 0x423ff0+ch), flags ' ' '#' '+' '-' '0', I64/h/l/w, %c %C %s %S %Z %d %i %u %o %x %X %p %n %e %f %g (through _cfltcvt_tab), write_char/write_multi_char/write_string, get_int_arg/get_int64_arg/get_short_arg, _wctomb, __aulldiv/__aullrem, __nullstring "(null)". argptr is the va_list (Ghidra undefined4 *). Not compiled (src/_crt_excluded); the host CRT's printf family replaces it.

name: stock_get_int_arg
note: CRT get_int_arg (output.c, static): reads an int from the va_list and advances it by 4. Only caller _output. Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_get_int64_arg
note: CRT get_int64_arg (output.c, static): reads an __int64 from the va_list and advances by 8 (_output, I64 modifier). Returns 8 bytes (undefined8), no allowed type, so no signature. Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_get_short_arg
note: CRT get_short_arg (output.c, static): reads a short (the wchar_t for %C) and advances the va_list by 4; _output passes the result to _wctomb. Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_callnewh
note: CRT _callnewh (handler.cpp): if _pnhHeap (0x00429458) is set, calls it with size and returns 1 when it returns nonzero, else 0. Caller realloc (0x00423950) retry loop. Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_heap_init
note: CRT _heap_init (heapinit.c): _crtheap = HeapCreate(HEAP_NO_SERIALIZE (1), 0x1000, 0). First call in entry (mainCRTStartup), before _ioinit; no small-block heap, no result check (older single-thread form). Compiled -> stock_ prefix.

name: stock_NLG_Notify
